questions.stem: If the pattern of the Koch Snowflake sequence continues, how many line segments will be in the fourth shape?
questions.solution: The Koch Snowflake increases the number of line segments by a factor of 4 at each step. Starting with 3 segments, the second shape has 12, the third has 48, and the fourth also has 48. The option 12 is the second shape, 3 is the first, and 144 is too large for the fourth step.

questions.stem: Which of the following number sequences is related to the number of corners in each shape of the Regular Polygons sequence?
choices: Counting numbers starting from 3
Counting numbers starting from 2

questions.solution: Regular polygons have the same number of corners as sides. The sequence of regular polygons starts with a triangle (3 sides/corners), then a square (4 sides/corners), and so on. questions.stem: If the pattern of adding odd numbers continues, what is the sum of the first 10 odd numbers?
questions.solution: The sum of the first n odd numbers is always n squared. For the first 10 odd numbers, this means 10 squared equals 100. The other options do not correspond to the square of any whole number and therefore do not follow the established pattern.

hi.stem: यदि विषम संख्याओं के जोड़ का पैटर्न जारी रहे, तो पहली 10 विषम संख्याओं का योग क्या है?

questions.stem: If a sequence of numbers is formed by adding the counting numbers up and then down, which of the following will be the next number in the sequence: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ...?
questions.solution: The sequence consists of square numbers, as each term is the square of an integer. The next square number after 36 is 49, which is 7 squared. The other options are squares of larger numbers and do not follow directly after 36.

hi.stem: यदि संख्याओं के एक अनुक्रम को गणना संख्याओं के ऊपर और फिर नीचे जोड़कर बनाया जाता है, तो निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी संख्या अनुक्रम में अगली होगी: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ...?

hi.critique: The translation accurately conveys the original meaning with appropriate mathematical terminology in Hindi.

questions.stem: If the number of little squares in each shape of the Stacked Squares sequence follows the pattern 1, 4, 9, 16, ..., what is the 12th term of this sequence?
questions.solution: The sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, ... represents the squares of the counting numbers. Each term is the square of its position in the sequence. The 12th term is 12 squared, which equals 144. The other options are not perfect squares of 12.
